overview: The original gold-standard sequencing method versus the massively parallel technology that eventually made whole genomes routine.
genZNote: One read at a time versus millions in parallel.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: A chain-termination method that sequences one DNA fragment (or a small number) per reaction, using dideoxynucleotides to stop synthesis at each base.
aspects.valueB: A family of high-throughput methods that sequence millions of DNA fragments in parallel, then reconstruct the full sequence computationally.

aspects.label: Throughput
aspects.valueA: Low — typically one sequence read (500–1000 bp) per capillary run.
aspects.valueB: Very high — millions to billions of reads generated per run.

aspects.label: Read Length
aspects.valueA: Long, highly accurate reads, up to roughly 1000 bp.
aspects.valueB: Historically shorter reads (commonly 100–300 bp for short-read platforms), though this varies by technology.

aspects.label: Cost per Base
aspects.valueA: High cost per base for large-scale sequencing.
aspects.valueB: Dramatically lower cost per base at scale, though instrument setup can be more expensive.

aspects.label: Per-Base Accuracy
aspects.valueA: Very high per-base accuracy, still considered the gold standard for confirming a specific variant.
aspects.valueB: High accuracy but with a wider range depending on platform and depends on adequate sequencing depth/coverage.

aspects.label: Data Analysis Complexity
aspects.valueA: Simple — each read can often be interpreted almost directly.
aspects.valueB: Complex — requires bioinformatics pipelines for read alignment, assembly, and variant calling across huge datasets.

aspects.label: Typical Applications
aspects.valueA: Confirming a single known mutation, small-scale targeted sequencing, quality control of cloned constructs.
aspects.valueB: Whole genome/exome sequencing, metagenomics, large-scale variant screening.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: Low-throughput, long, highly accurate single reads.
aspects.valueB: Massively parallel, high-throughput sequencing of many fragments at once.
